description_good_justification: README.md opens with what Axmem is: a standalone memory server for AI agents, built as an MCP server on FastMCP. https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem#readme
interact_justification: The README says how to get Axmem (Quick Start, Installing the package: PyPI or source) and has a Contributing section that points to https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md for feedback and contributions.
contribution_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md (ways to contribute, setup, making a change: fork, branch, tests, pull request against main) and https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md.
contribution_requirements_justification: The requirements for acceptable contributions (layering, typing and style tools, tests, 100 percent coverage, commit format, dependencies, package contents) are in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#rules-for-code, with the tool details in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md.
floss_license_justification: Axmem is AGPL-3.0-only (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/LICENSE); the code derived from Forgetful keeps its MIT notice (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/LICENSE-FORGETFUL-MIT.md).
floss_license_osi_justification: AGPL-3.0-only and MIT are both approved by the Open Source Initiative.
license_location_justification: The license is in the top-level file https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/LICENSE; the MIT notice of the upstream project is in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/LICENSE-FORGETFUL-MIT.md.
documentation_basics_justification: The README has Quick Start, Authentication and tenants, Qdrant and Connecting to an Agent (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem#quick-start); the guides are in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/.
documentation_interface_justification: The MCP tools are in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/tool_reference.md, the REST API in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/api_reference.md, the settings in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/configuration.md and the command line in the CLI section of the README.
sites_https_justification: The project site (github.com/Axiumine/axmem), the package index page (pypi.org/project/axmem) and the file host (files.pythonhosted.org) are served over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests, which are threaded and public: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/issues
english_justification: The documentation, code comments and commit messages are in English, and the project takes issues and pull requests in English.
repo_track_justification: git records what changed, who changed it and when.
repo_interim_justification: Every commit is pushed to the public main branch between releases, not only the release commits.
repo_distributed_justification: git is a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version and a tag (v0.6.0rc1); hatch-vcs derives the package version from the tag.
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged in git as v<version>; the release flow in docs/release.md pushes the tag and the signing workflow runs on it.
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog: one section per release with Added, Changed, Removed, Fixed and Security entries, and the reason for each change is in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/changes-from-forgetful.md.
report_process_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ways-to-contribute says how to report a bug or request a feature in the issue tracker and what to include.
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/issues?q=
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The process for reporting a vulnerability is published in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/SECURITY.md: what to report, how to report it privately, the targets for a first answer and a fix plan, which versions receive fixes, and how a fix and its disclosure proceed. README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link to it.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: A private report goes through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, which is enabled for the repository (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/security/advisories/new, over HTTPS), or by e-mail to the lead maintainer; both ways are described in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/SECURITY.md, which asks reporters not to open a public issue.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known run-time vulnerability of Axmem itself has been fixed in a release, so there is none to list: the project has no CVE and no published security advisory. Advisories of dependencies that a version bump fixed are recorded in the Security section of https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md; a vulnerability of Axmem that is fixed in future will be listed in the release notes.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months: the repository has no security advisory, no issue and no Dependabot alert. https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/SECURITY.md sets the targets for a first answer (7 days) and a fix plan (14 days).
build_justification: The package is built with hatchling and hatch-vcs ([build-system] in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/pyproject.toml); the release rebuilds it from the tag (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/release.md#what-the-release-guarantees).
build_common_tools_justification: hatchling (PEP 517) driven by uv, both in common use for Python packages.
build_floss_tools_justification: uv, hatchling, hatch-vcs and pytest are FLOSS; the build needs no GPU or proprietary tool.
test_justification: A pytest suite in tests/ (architecture, integration, end-to-end); how to run it is in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/contributors.md#testing-philosophy and https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change.
test_invocation_justification: The suites run in the standard way for Python, with pytest through uv, for example uv run pytest tests/integration/: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/contributors.md#testing-philosophy
test_most_justification: Branch coverage of app/ and main.py is measured and must be 100 percent ([tool.coverage] in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/pyproject.toml, the coverage gate in docs/quality-gates.md).
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change (make the change, with tests) and https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#rules-for-code: new functionality comes with automated tests, and a change to code without the tests that prove it is not merged.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major changes ship with tests, for example scripts/smoke-release.sh with tests/integration/test_release_smoke_script*.py and the fuzz harnesses with tests/integration/test_fuzz_targets.py; the changelog entries name them: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
tests_documented_added_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change, step 2 (make the change, with tests), and https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review.
warnings_justification: ruff, mypy and pylint look for code quality errors, and pytest turns warnings into errors: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/ruff.toml, [tool.mypy] and [tool.pylint] in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/pyproject.toml, and https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/pytest.ini. ruff, mypy and pylint run as gates in the pre-commit hook and in hosted CI; the test suites run in the pre-push hook. Ruff enforces 140 columns and pylint 100 under fail-under 8.0; the pre-commit hook runs pylint on the staged files without the convention checks, so the 100 columns are counted only by the project-wide run in the pre-push hook and in hosted CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: The pre-commit and pre-push hooks and the quality.yml workflow fail on any finding of these tools, so a change cannot be committed or merged with one; an exception is explained in the code or the pull request (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#rules-for-code).
warnings_strict_justification: The project turns on the warning flags of its tools wherever that is practical, and what it leaves off is listed in the configuration files with the reason and the count of findings. ruff selects 54 rule groups, among them pycodestyle (E, W, with lines of at most 140 columns), pep8-naming, bugbear, flake8-bandit (S), tryceratops, pathlib, mccabe and the pylint groups, and a suppression is a '# noqa: <code> - reason' on one line (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/ruff.toml). mypy runs in strict mode with warn_unreachable, warn_unused_ignores, disallow_any_unimported and nine optional error codes, and pylint must score 8/10 with eleven more extensions loaded ([tool.mypy] and [tool.pylint] in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/pyproject.toml). pytest turns every warning into an error (filterwarnings = error) with one ignore line, limited to one message, one category and one module, for a deprecation that a pinned third-party library raises when it is imported (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/pytest.ini), and two narrower ones in the tests: two marks that each ignore one message, and one fixture in tests/conftest.py that ignores one UserWarning while it builds a client for the loopback test node. Not enabled, honestly: in ruff, TRY003 (356 findings), PT011 (87), G004 (28) and PLC0415 (207), and PLR2004 in the tests only (939 findings there; it is on in the code), each off with its reason in ruff.toml, and the groups ANN (about 15900 findings, mostly in the tests; mypy strict requires annotations in the code it checks), D (about 5900), EM (384), FBT (120), TC (about 230), T20 (185), INP (393) and the preview rules CPY (about 550) and DOC (about 1200), which are not selected because fixing them would change signatures, the output of the CLI or types that pydantic and FastAPI need at run time; in mypy, redundant-expr (3 findings), truthy-bool (2) and explicit-override (18), and test_harness is not type-checked (33 strict errors); ruff enforces 140 columns and pylint 100 under the 8/10 threshold, which stays because the score is 8.00 and most of its findings are lines over 100 columns; the pre-commit hook runs pylint on the staged files without the convention checks, so those 100 columns are counted only in the pre-push hook and in hosted CI. The gates run in the pre-commit and pre-push hooks and, for the static ones, in hosted CI, and no threshold is lowered to make a change pass: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md#warnings.
crypto_published_justification: Axmem implements no cryptography. It uses SHA-256 (hashlib) for token hashes and cache keys, hmac.compare_digest, and the JWT and TLS code of FastMCP, authlib, httpx, uvicorn and OpenSSL.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic work is done by hashlib, hmac, FastMCP's JWT verification and the TLS stack of httpx and OpenSSL (uvicorn passes the certificate, the key and the cipher string of https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/app/config/tls.py to OpenSSL when the server serves TLS); app/ re-implements none of it.
crypto_floss_justification: Everything that depends on cryptography uses the Python standard library and FLOSS libraries.
crypto_keylength_justification: Axmem generates no cryptographic keys and chooses no key length: JWT keys come from the operator's identity provider and static tokens are matched by SHA-256 digest.
crypto_working_justification: A search of app/ and main.py finds no MD4, MD5, DES or RC4, and no SHA-1 used for anything but identifiers. The hash used for security is SHA-256 (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/app/middleware/static_token.py; also file checksums and the engine-cache fingerprint). SHA-1 appears in one place only: uuid.uuid5 derives non-secret identifiers, the id of a link between two memories (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/app/repositories/qdrant/payloads.py) and the id of a tenant from its name (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/app/models/tenant_models.py). A UUIDv5 is not used for a signature, a password, a token or an integrity check, and nothing relies on it being secret.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No weak algorithm or CBC mode is used by the security mechanisms of app/ and main.py; static tokens are SHA-256 digests compared with hmac.compare_digest. The only SHA-1 is inside uuid.uuid5, which derives identifiers (see crypto_working), not a security mechanism.
crypto_pfs_justification: Axmem implements no key agreement protocol itself, but when SERVER_SSL_CERTFILE and SERVER_SSL_KEYFILE are set, the TLS of its HTTP server (OpenSSL, through uvicorn) agrees keys only in forward-secret ways: TLS 1.3, whose suites are all forward secret, and for TLS 1.2 only ECDHE with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 (TLS_CIPHERS in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/app/config/tls.py). https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/tests/integration/test_tls_server.py negotiates TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2 on a real socket and shows that an RSA key exchange and the ECDHE CBC-SHA1 suites are refused. Without those settings the server speaks plain HTTP, which is the default, and has no key agreement of its own; behind a TLS-terminating proxy the proxy's policy applies. Axmem's own clients use the default TLS stack.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Axmem stores no passwords of external users. It authenticates bearer tokens: a static token is configured as a SHA-256 digest of a random token, and JWT and introspection are delegated to the identity provider (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/security.md).
crypto_random_justification: Axmem generates no cryptographic keys or nonces. uuid4 is used for non-secret identifiers only, and an operator makes a static token with openssl rand as the README shows.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are delivered from PyPI and GitHub Releases over HTTPS, signed with cosign (keyless) and attested with SLSA provenance; PEP 740 attestations are on PyPI.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No script, workflow or hook fetches a hash or a file over plain http; digests are in git (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/release-digests.json) and checked with signatures (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/release.md#checking-a-release).
no_leaked_credentials_justification: GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled on the repository. A scan of the whole git history for private keys and common token formats (cloud, GitHub, PyPI and Hugging Face tokens) found no credential, the local environment file is git-ignored and untracked (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/.gitignore), and the example file holds placeholders only.
static_analysis_justification: bandit, Semgrep (local rules plus the p/python and p/security-audit packs), ruff (54 rule groups, the security S rules among them), pylint, mypy, vulture, radon and trivy run on every push and pull request (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/.github/workflows/quality.yml) and in the git hooks; the release guard requires CI to be green on the release commit (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/release.md).
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: bandit, Semgrep (p/security-audit and local rules in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/.semgrep/axmem.yml) and the flake8-bandit (S) rules of ruff look for common vulnerabilities; trivy scans dependencies, secrets and misconfiguration. CodeQL also analyses the Python code and the workflow files on GitHub, on a push to main and on pull requests into main, as a report (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The hooks and quality.yml fail on a finding of these tools, so it is fixed or explained before the change is committed or merged (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md); a threshold is not weakened to make a gate pass (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/AGENTS.md).
static_analysis_often_justification: quality.yml runs on every push and pull request to any branch, and bandit, Semgrep, ruff, mypy and pylint also run in the pre-commit hook.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The pre-push hook, which every release push passes (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/release.md), runs the end-to-end suites with pytest-memray memory budgets and the Atheris fuzz harnesses of fuzz/ (a short run each; longer runs are by hand): https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/fuzzing.md. The harnesses cover token claims, tool-argument coercion and terminal text, not the HTTP surface.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Axmem is pure Python (a memory-safe language) and has no C or C++ code of its own.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The pre-push hook fails on a finding of the memory budgets or the fuzz harnesses, and https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/fuzzing.md#when-a-harness-fails says a harness failure is fixed in the code with a regression test.
governance_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md: roles, how decisions are made, how changes are reviewed, access, and what happens if the lead is unavailable.
code_of_conduct_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1), with the maintainers as contacts (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md).
roles_responsibilities_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles defines the lead maintainer, the co-owner and successor, contributors and reporters; https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md says who holds which role.
documentation_roadmap_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md covers November 2026 to October 2027 and lists what the project plans and what it does not plan to do.
documentation_architecture_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/architecture.md: component view, entry points, MCP/HTTP/identity, write and retrieval paths, and the import boundaries that tests enforce.
documentation_security_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/security.md lists what a user can and cannot expect: numbered requirements with the code that enforces them and the tests that prove them, and an explicit list of what Axmem does not guarantee.
documentation_quick_start_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/README.md#quick-start: install from source or from PyPI, run, and connect an agent.
documentation_current_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/AGENTS.md requires CHANGELOG.md and docs/changes-from-forgetful.md to be updated in every commit that changes behaviour, and tests/integration/test_reference_docs.py and test_install_requirements.py keep the README and the guides in step with the code.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: Axmem is a headless MCP server with a REST API and a command-line tool. It has no graphical or web interface, and its documentation is Markdown on GitHub.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub and PyPI, which handle accounts. Axmem stores no passwords of external users (static tokens are configured as SHA-256 digests).
coding_standards_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards names PEP 8, PEP 484 type hints and the Python 3.14 idioms checked by ruff's UP rules, says the tool configuration wins where it differs, and the gates fail a change that does not comply. ruff enforces PEP 8 with its pycodestyle (E, W), pep8-naming (N) and isort (I) groups, and the line length is checked by ruff at 140 columns (E501) and by pylint at 100 under its 8/10 threshold (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/ruff.toml).
build_standard_variables_justification: Axmem is a pure-Python wheel built by hatchling; nothing is compiled, so there are no compiler or linker variables to honour.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Axmem is a pure-Python package with no compiled code and no stripping step.
build_non_recursive_justification: One non-recursive hatchling build of one package ([build-system] and [tool.hatch.build.targets] in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/pyproject.toml).
build_repeatable_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/release.md#what-the-release-guarantees: release.yml rebuilds at a fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from release-digests.json and refuses to sign unless the rebuild is byte-identical; the build backend is pinned to exact versions.
installation_common_justification: Axmem is a PyPI package: uv tool install or pip install (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/README.md#installing-the-package), removed with uv tool uninstall axmem or pip uninstall axmem (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/connectivity_guide.md).
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is done by pip or uv, which choose the location (--prefix, --target, --root); Axmem has no install script and writes nothing outside its package at install time.
installation_development_quick_justifica: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up: git clone, uv sync --locked --all-extras --dev, and scripts.quality install for the hooks.
external_dependencies_justification: Dependencies are listed in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/pyproject.toml (the runtime dependencies, the dev and harness groups and the build backend, each pinned to an exact version with ==) and locked with hashes in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/uv.lock.
dependency_monitoring_justification: The trivy gate scans the locked dependencies for known vulnerabilities on every push and pull request (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/.github/workflows/quality.yml) and in the pre-push hook; fixes are recorded in the Security section of https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md. Dependabot version updates are configured in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: All dependencies come from package indexes through pyproject.toml and uv.lock; app/ and main.py hold no vendored or forked copy of a library.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: ci.yml runs the architecture test suite on every push and pull request, with pass or fail in GitHub Actions. The suites that need the GPU and Docker run in the pre-push hook of the maintainer's machine, as https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md says.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: coverage.py with branch coverage and fail_under = 100 ([tool.coverage.report] in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/pyproject.toml); the coverage gate runs in the pre-push hook.
test_policy_mandated_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#rules-for-code (tests; coverage 100 percent) and https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review: a change to code without the tests that prove it is not merged.
assurance_case_justification: https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md: threat model, trust boundaries, an argument for the secure design principles (Saltzer and Schroeder), the OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25 tables, and the residual risks.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: Credentials (the Qdrant API key, provider keys, the hash of a static token, JWT keys) come from environment variables or a dotenv settings file, not from the code (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/configuration.md); they are replaced by editing the setting and restarting the server.
crypto_tls12_justification: With SERVER_SSL_CERTFILE and SERVER_SSL_KEYFILE set, the HTTP server accepts TLS 1.2 or later only, with forward-secret cipher suites only (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/app/config/tls.py; https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/tests/integration/test_tls_server.py checks the minimum version and the versions and suites that a real client negotiates). Without them the server serves plain HTTP, which is the default, and expects a TLS-terminating proxy in front. Axmem implements no TLS itself: OpenSSL does the work, through uvicorn for the server and through Python 3.14's default SSL context, which requires TLS 1.2 or later, for its own clients (httpx, qdrant-client and the provider SDKs).
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: No code in app/ or main.py turns off certificate verification (no verify=False, CERT_NONE or check_hostname override); the default verification of httpx and the SDKs applies. https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/tests/integration/test_tls_server.py runs the client of the CLI (fastmcp.Client, through RemoteExecutor) against a TLS server: it refuses a certificate from an unknown authority, also when SSL_CERT_FILE names another authority, and connects only when SSL_CERT_FILE names the authority of the server.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The default clients verify the certificate in the TLS handshake, before any HTTP header is sent, and Axmem has no override.
signed_releases_justification: Each release file is signed with cosign (keyless, so no private key exists) and attested with SLSA provenance; PyPI also carries PEP 740 attestations. How to verify is in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/release.md#checking-a-release.
input_validation_justification: Typed models with bounds validate every MCP argument and REST body, query parameters are parsed strictly, a body limit answers 413 and malformed input is a 4xx, never a 500: requirement NET-3 in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/security.md, proved by tests/e2e/test_request_bounds_e2e.py.
hardening_justification: The HTTP server sets security headers on every answer of the application, the refusals included (not a 500 from an unhandled exception, nor the 400 that uvicorn itself sends for malformed HTTP): Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control no-store, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy, and Strict-Transport-Security when it serves TLS (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/app/middleware/security_headers.py, tested in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/tests/integration/test_security_headers.py). When SERVER_SSL_CERTFILE and SERVER_SSL_KEYFILE are set (plain HTTP is the default), its TLS offers TLS 1.2 or later and forward-secret authenticated cipher suites only (https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/app/config/tls.py).
copyright_per_file_justification: Every source file (Python, shell scripts, Git hooks, workflows, Dockerfile) starts with an SPDX-FileCopyrightText line naming the holder: Giovanni Manzoni, and Scott Raisbeck for files derived from Forgetful. Files that cannot hold a comment are covered by https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/REUSE.toml. The reuse quality gate fails a commit, a push and the hosted run when a file has no notice; see https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md#licensing-headers.
license_per_file_justification: Every source file starts with SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only, or AGPL-3.0-only AND MIT for a file derived from Forgetful, and the license texts are in https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/LICENSES/. Files that cannot hold a comment are covered by https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/REUSE.toml. The reuse quality gate fails a commit, a push and the hosted run when a file has no license; see https://github.com/Axiumine/axmem/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md#licensing-headers.
